_comment: Source-of-truth mapping for Cloudflare AI Gateway dynamic-route model tiers. Apps call a TIER name via model:"dynamic/<tier>", never a raw model id. The free-tier provider is PRIMARY: its key is stored in the gateway as a BYOK provider key, so those calls bill the provider's own free quota instead of Cloudflare unified-billing credits, and fail over to the paid provider automatically when the free tier 429s. No API key is ever sent in a request — runtime auth is the cf-aig-authorization header only.
gateway_notes: authentication=true AND store_id shared with the account's default gateway are both required. That store binding is what enables keyless Unified Billing on a NON-default gateway. Read your default gateway's store_id from GET /accounts/{account_id}/ai-gateway/gateways/default and reuse the value here.

code.purpose: OPTIONAL third tier — top-end code/agentic work, quality over cost

notes.azure: Azure OpenAI CANNOT be a route step. The dynamic-route model element has no field for Azure's resource name / api-version / BYOK key, so an azure-openai step 500s at runtime. Reach Azure via the direct provider path instead. Verified by scripts/test-routing.sh step 5.
notes.code_tier: The `code` tier deliberately falls back to a second model from the SAME provider — no cross-provider top-end code model was verified equivalent. Reduced provider diversity is an accepted trade-off there.
notes.tier_count: Two tiers (low + high) cover essentially every user-facing app path. Add `code` only if you genuinely need frontier reasoning in production.

verification.failover_proof: A throwaway route with a deliberately bogus primary model fell back to the secondary and returned HTTP 200, while a bad-only control route (no fallback) errored. Route deleted after the test. Reproduce with scripts/test-routing.sh.
